findings.text: The task only asked for two new functions in `tinydb.operations`. This diff also rewrites the core of `Table.update`: it deep-copies every document, buffers the results in `pending`, and commits them at the end. That changes the behaviour of every callable update for all users, and it adds a deepcopy cost per document. None of it is covered by a test, and the task didn't ask for it. `push` and `pull` work without it, so revert it. If the atomicity change is wanted, make it a separate, reviewed change.

The new copy-and-commit behaviour is only applied to `update`. `update_multiple` still calls `fields(table[doc_id])` in place, so the two methods now behave differently on a failing callable. The non-callable path in `update` is also not atomic. The comment and the claim that failures leave no partial writes are therefore only partly true.

The new tests don't cover `push` or `pull` on a document that lacks the field or holds a non-list. They also don't cover a multi-document update. The existing `db` fixture is not used for the list cases, which insert their own documents.

This change to `Table.update` wasn't requested. The task was two new functions in `operations.py`. The deep-copy and `pending` commit rewrite of the core update path adds a full `deepcopy` of every updated document and changes semantics for all callable updates. It should be dropped, or split into its own change.

Regression for duplicate IDs. `update(push(...), doc_ids=[1, 1])` used to apply the function twice, because `updated_ids` keeps the duplicates and the old code mutated in place. Now each call deep-copies the not-yet-committed `table[doc_id]`, so the second result overwrites the first in `pending` and the function takes effect only once. This is a silent behaviour change for any callable, including `increment` and `push`.

`update_multiple` still calls `fields(table[doc_id])` in place. So `push` and `pull` behave differently there than in `update`, and the new all-or-nothing guarantee only applies to `update`. If the guarantee is wanted, it is applied inconsistently.

The tests only cover one document with a pre-existing list. They don't cover several matching documents, a pull on a list that ends up empty, or the new atomic-update behaviour added in `table.py`. That behaviour has no test, nor does the duplicate-ID case it changes.
